tip: 보다 (boda) attaches to the thing you compare AGAINST, not the winner: 기차보다 빨라요 (gicha-boda ppallayo) = faster than the train. 'Than' comes after its noun in Korean.
덜 (deol) = less, dropped right before the adjective: 덜 짜요 (deol jjayo) = less salty. Korean has no '-er' endings – degree words like 덜 and 더 (deo = more) sit before the plain adjective.
처럼 (cheoreom) means 'like' but glues onto the END of its noun: 천사처럼 자요 (cheonsa-cheoreom jayo) = sleeps like an angel. English puts 'like' before – Korean always after.
제일 (jeil) and 가장 (gajang) both mean 'most' – 제일 is the everyday spoken choice: 제일 바빠요 (jeil bappayo) = is the busiest.
